comparator.name: Communication Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-taught variant has 90 EC of taught foundations and disciplinary work, 30 EC of free electives, 58 EC of integrative work and 2 EC of tutoring and portfolio work. The example uses the Corporate Communication graduation project and two topics.
components: Topic Say hi to AI: the role of AI in strategic communication
Topic Algorithmic Persuasion in the Digital Society

routeSelection.basis: The Dutch programme target leaves the project domain open. Corporate Communication is the first project listed in the dated catalogue. The example uses the first-listed topic in each of the first two blocks of the last semester after the first-semester electives. This selection was made independently of UCR alignment.

core: Communication theory, media, persuasion and effects on people and society
Quantitative, qualitative and experimental communication research
Corporate, entertainment, persuasive and political communication domains
adjacent: Corporate, persuasive, marketing and health communication
questions: How do media and communication affect people, behaviour and society?
How can messages and communication strategies achieve organisational, health or social goals?
How do journalism, political communication and media trust shape democracy?

candidates.label: Media, political communication and public trust
Entertainment Communication & Audience Behaviour
candidates.reason: This is a coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included and the closest match retains substantial entertainment-media coverage.

candidates.label: Global & Intercultural Communication
candidates.reason: This is a coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included; the normalized Dutch track does not prioritize the distinct English Global Communication Science track.

alternatives.label: Communication, media and society
alternatives.concept: Studies how media and messages shape behaviour and society. It combines rhetoric, persuasion and media analysis with quantitative and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: Rhetoric, media analysis and research foundations precede work on persuasion, media representation and documentary. Experimental methods precedes advanced evidence synthesis.
progression: Rhetoric, media analysis and research foundations precede work on persuasion, media representation and documentary. Experimental methods precedes advanced evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Persuasion, marketing and health behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: Research methods and business foundations support marketing, market research and strategy. Social psychology, epidemiology and medical psychology add a health-behaviour strand.
alternatives.concept: Studies how organisations communicate with audiences and try to influence decisions. Marketing, consumer research and persuasion are central. Psychology and public health provide contexts for studying health behaviour.
progression: Research methods and business foundations support marketing, market research and strategy. Social psychology, epidemiology and medical psychology add a health-behaviour strand.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes behaviour, health and marketing the application domains for persuasion and communication; it differs from the broad closest match by more than four courses and 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Media, political communication and public trust
alternatives.concept: Studies how political institutions, media and public debate shape trust and participation. Documentary, political analysis and social research offer different ways to examine public communication.
alternatives.labelReason: Media and comparative politics foundations precede documentary, policy analysis and European politics. Social theory and qualitative and quantitative methods support research on public debate.
alternatives.distinctness: This route centres democratic politics, journalism and public trust; it differs from both the broad communication pathway and the health-focused pathway by more than four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Media and comparative politics foundations precede documentary, policy analysis and European politics. Social theory and qualitative and quantitative methods support research on public debate.

blocks: Both study how messages influence people. UCR applies persuasion techniques in a community project.
Both study entertainment media and how audiences engage with them. UCR examines representation and cultural history.
UCR courses address rhetoric, media and social behaviour separately. UvA introduces communication science across these areas.
UCR media courses examine technologies, representation and history. UvA focuses on media industries, markets and regulation.
UCR addresses digital strategy, but the selected courses do not dedicate a course to AI in strategic communication.
UCR studies persuasion and digital media in separate courses. UvA applies communication research to algorithmic targeting and influence.
Both use evidence to develop practical recommendations. UCR focuses on marketing and consumer engagement.
Both develop survey design, measurement and data analysis through a practical research project.
Both examine relationships inside organisations. UvA also studies how organisations communicate with external stakeholders.
Both teach qualitative research design and interpretation through social research.
UCR combines politics, rhetoric and documentary practice. UvA studies how news media, journalists, audiences and politics interact.
Both develop experimental design and analysis. UCR applies them to health and behaviour, while UvA studies communication effects.
Both support academic skills and reflection. UvA’s tutor and portfolio activities run through the first three semesters.
UCR research methods and statistics are used in separate comparisons with the survey and experiment courses.
Some UCR courses examine evidence and ethical reasoning. UvA gives philosophy of science and methodology dedicated attention.
UCR media analysis and data science offer related skills. UvA requires practical quantitative media content analysis.
UCR advanced research methods focuses on meta-analysis. UvA teaches statistical reasoning across communication research.
Some UCR courses include projects with external partners. UvA requires a separate supervised internship with research.
This is approved open elective space.
UvA requires a graduation project and individual thesis. UCR’s independent research element is optional.

selection.assessment: The broad communication option integrates media, persuasion and social research. The marketing and behaviour option concentrates on organisational decisions and audience research. The political option adds public institutions, policy and documentary practice. All are distinct, and three options reach the limit. Entertainment is substantially represented within the closest option. The intercultural topic does not change the chosen Dutch target.

notes.text: UCR offers communication, media and social research across several subjects. UvA has a linked sequence of survey, content analysis and experimental research, plus a required internship and graduation project.

audience.programmeDescription: Communication Science at the University of Amsterdam studies how media and messages influence people, organisations and society. The Dutch-taught programme combines communication research with an internship and a graduation project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines media, persuasion and research. The other options focus on marketing and behaviour, or on media and political communication.

componentNotes.y2-tutorial: Tutoring and portfolio work run across the first three semesters. The 2 EC are awarded after completion.
componentNotes.y3-project: The Corporate Communication project includes team data collection and an individual thesis.
